summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge: analyze Soony's launch data, find hidden risks, and build a general product (Lighthouse) that watches portal drops, recomputes feasibility, and takes approved actions, then polish and demo it before the hand-in.
summary.outcome: Found that the Collector's Edition misses launch (art book overbooking, failed statues, etc.) despite an 'ok' plan, wrote briefing pages and interview docs, built a poller/agent/UI with case flow, routines, logo and bell menu, and set up a no-login demo at lighthouse.stenglein.dev with a saved story state. Most work is committed on main but not pushed; live not restarted.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhooks or notifications. Changes must be detected by polling the list and comparing SHA-256, since files get replaced under the same name.
Confidential portal data lives in gitignored data/ and .env; .env.example is committed. Findings notes are kept locally in data/notes/.
The API server does not load .env on import, so settings like ASK_VIEWER_TITLE need a helper that loads .env first, and a restart.

Routine steps are only valid for certain watched kinds: 'chase once if no answer' needs waiting-for-reply routines and 'ask for a status' needs shipment routines. The server rejects them on decision routines (clean_spec).
The case-flow and routine diagram share connector and node components exported from FlowGraph.tsx so they cannot drift apart.

Demo instance is run via scripts/demo.sh (restart, save-story, story). Open mode is ASK_DEMO_OPEN=on ASK_DEMO_HOST=lighthouse.stenglein.dev. Servers and the Cloudflare tunnel run in tmux on the Mac, with caffeinate to prevent sleep.
Team workflow lives in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md in the repo; tasks are claimed with a Now line in PROGRESS.md.
Number keys 1-9 only choose an option and Cmd+Enter carries out the chosen one. Option 1 is the recommended one and is preselected.
workflow: Entire hooks only write a checkpoint when repo files change, so a session with no repo changes shows 'skipping checkpoint' even though hooks fired.
Subagents worked well for bulk cross-checking (200 order confirmations and 59 scans) and for drawing logo variants without touching the repo.
Verify UI changes with headless screenshots at phone, desktop and 1080p sizes; measure pixel positions rather than guessing alignment (logo vs text was resolved by measuring ink rows).
Interrupted tool calls often still land their commits, so check git state after an interrupt.
Restarting the Cloudflare tunnel takes every hostname down for about a minute, and a wrong tmux session name made the first restart fail.

friction: The token was initially empty, which blocked the data pull until the user supplied it.

Phone layout of the case flow went through many iterations: two-column snake order, empty-looking folded state, overlapping bottom bar, auto-scroll on load, and Details looking identical to the compact view.
The Add step menu offered steps that the server then rejected, which looked like a bug.
The top bar got crowded after adding the role and status text and needed a 3-column grid.
The logo nudge went the wrong direction first and needed measurement to fix.
The tunnel restart briefly took live, demo and lighthouse offline, and the first tmux restart attempt failed.
The demo state had drifted (only 5 cases open, art books and rev B gone) and had to be reset from the snapshot.
The hand-in time changed from 12:00 to 12:45 mid-session, and the assistant repeatedly asked to push main without receiving an answer.
open_items: Push main (about 30 commits ahead of origin) and restart live so the sign-in choice, Senior Buyer title, heartbeat and other changes appear there.
User still has to record the demo video (about 2.5 min) and cover the deck; the assistant prepared the story state and cannot do the voice-over.
Register sender email addresses in portal Settings, then send the Karton Nowak art book order (offer valid 24h) and reply to Boise about EXW terms.
Support 'send email, then chase once if no answer' on decision routines via a follow-up that watches for replies.
Routines page is cluttered: make a compact list with details on demand, a ⋯ menu, and a merge hint for duplicate routines.
Optionally make all cases on phone a bottom sheet from the top bar; considered and deferred until after the hand-in.
Open question whether portal data differs between teams and whether our actions create new portal files; ask the Lio engineers.
Consider moving the demo from the Mac to ada if it must run without the laptop (about 30 minutes); the old Claude doc is still there and the user has not decided whether to delete it.
The 'Ask Maren to approve' button jumping could not be reproduced; need to find where it happens.
